introH2: 🗺️ Can you do Tak on a small budget — and which area should you base yourself in?
introHtml: Tak is a big province most people pass through rather than plan a trip around — driving north, heading to Mae Sot for cross-border errands, or pushing on to Umphang for the Thee Lor Su waterfall. The good news is that Tak hides far more good-value stays in the low hundreds to low thousands of baht than most people expect, and plenty of them are genuinely worth it. The key to doing Tak on a budget is to match your base to your plans, because the main draws are in different districts — riverside Tak town on the Ping River is the base for a stopover and town sightseeing, with in-town hotels a walk from the river and market, plus garden resorts by the highway that get you straight back on the road · Mae Sot district, about 80 km away, is the border town with the most — and newest — budget stays in the province: budget chains, small boutiques and owner-run guesthouses · and Umphang is far out, where most stays are nature resorts priced above the budget range, so we focus on the first two areas. This guide rounds up 10 budget stays in Tak we've reviewed, every one scoring 8.0 or higher, ranked by value — not just the cheapest, but weighing the score, the number of real reviews, and what you get per baht. Each comes from reading real guest reviews, with the honest pros and cons, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Tak has no metro and no train, so you get around by car, and the province is spread out enough that your choice of area sets up the whole trip. Stays in Tak town (Nai Wiang) are the easiest, some within walking distance of the Ping River, the evening market and restaurants (Berich, Silayok). Edge-of-town / riverside stays on the Mae Tho and Nam Rueam side trade walkability for quiet and big car parks, but you need a car to reach the centre (Tak Andaman, Pingview, Suansin). Mae Sot stays sit mostly along the Asian Highway in the town centre, near markets, the border crossing and Mae Sot Airport (Hop Inn, B2, One Budget), while the small boutiques and guesthouses in Mae Pa are more on the edge and need a car (Moeimanee, RETRO). The areas in this guide: Tak Town — riverside, town sightseeing, road-trip stopovers · Mae Sot — border, Rim Moei market, airport · for the edge-of-town and Mae Sot stays a car is recommended, as public transport is scarce and nearby shops close early.

entries.storyHtml: We rank Berich Hotel the best value in this guide because it stacks a high score of 8.7, a big 1,335 reviews and a low ฿690 rate all in one place. It's a minimal-style hotel in central Tak town on Mahat Thai Bamrung Road, and what sets it apart from the usual cheap stay is that every room is the same roomy ~32 sqm, styled in white-grey-gold, with breakfast included, free parking and a lift. Real guest reviews praise the rooms being bigger than the price suggests, clean, with comfy beds and friendly staff, plus a walk to the King Taksin Shrine and the Ping River suspension bridge. The trade-offs: there's no pool, breakfast is à la carte with limited choice in a small dining area, some beds are firm, and a few rooms use a key-card power system. Best for people driving through Tak and in town on errands who want a new, roomy, central room on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you like a soft mattress, ask for an extra pillow at check-in, as some beds are firm. The free breakfast has limited choice — eat light, then head out for noodles in town. Want a city or mountain view? Ask for floor 4–5 when booking. If you need the fridge running all day, check how the key-card power works first.

entries.storyHtml: Tak Andaman Resort & Hotel is the most-reviewed stay in this guide, with 3,428 reviews — a resort in a big garden on Phahonyothin Road in Mae Tho, about 5 km from Tak town, scoring 8.2 from ฿750. Its draw is the quiet, leafy setting, with houses and villas in several sizes from twin rooms to three-bedroom houses, and a big car park where you park right outside your room. Real guest reviews praise the shady garden, roomy rooms, friendly staff, and a location that gets you straight back on the highway — ideal as a stopover on the Bangkok–Chiang Mai–Mae Sot–Sukhothai route. The trade-offs: the place is showing its age, with some dated furniture, air-con that isn't ice-cold in a few rooms, a 5 km distance from town that all but requires a car, and pool info that differs by site, so check first. Best for road-trippers and families or groups who want space on a budget.

entries.storyHtml: Pingview Villa Resort is a low-priced Ping River stay that sells atmosphere and warmth more than polished rooms, from just ฿500, with a big 1,421 reviews (Agoda around 8.5). It started as a riverside food garden serving fresh Ping River fish with live music, then added riverside rooms to sleep in, out in Mae Tho. Real guest reviews praise the quiet riverside setting and pretty views, roomy rooms for the price, warm staff, and being one of the few pet-friendly stays in Tak. The honest trade-offs: room upkeep is inconsistent, with some rooms showing bathroom mould or missing amenities, breakfast is minimal, and noise from the food garden and karaoke reaches nearby rooms on some nights — so TripAdvisor scores it lower than the booking sites. Best for travellers with a car who value a riverside setting, a low price and bringing a pet over spotless rooms.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Room quality is a bit of a lottery — ask about the room's condition and for recent photos, and pick a free-cancellation rate. Light sleeper? Ask for a room away from the food garden and karaoke. Want a river view? Ask for a room with a Ping River balcony. Focus on dinner in the riverside food garden rather than the breakfast.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate from-rates for standard rooms out of peak season and can change by date and season; always check live prices and compare 3 sites before booking. The scores and standouts here come from reading real guest reviews on the booking platforms — we didn't stay ourselves. Every stay here scores 8.0+, but these are budget 2–3-star places, so they come with limits: most have no pool, some rooms are small, and some sit on the edge of town or by the highway, out of walking range of the sights — read each one's honest notes before booking. In particular, Pingview Villa Resort has inconsistent room upkeep (booking sites score it well from many reviews, but TripAdvisor lower) — ask about the room's condition and pick a free-cancellation rate. All 10 stays can be booked and price-compared across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com. We focus on Tak town and Mae Sot, as most Umphang stays are nature resorts priced above the budget range. Tak has no metro and little public transport, so a car is recommended for the edge-of-town and Mae Sot stays. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about budget Tak hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best-value budget hotel in Tak?
faq.a: Weighing value (score + number of real reviews + what you get per baht), Berich Hotel ฿690 is the best value in this guide — every room a roomy 32 sqm with breakfast included, scoring 8.7 from a big 1,335 reviews, in central Tak town. For the cheapest, Silayok Grand Hotel ฿450 (8.1 · TripAdvisor #2 in Tak) and B2 Mae Sot ฿550 (budget chain, 8.7) are strong value. The highest score in the set is Hop Inn Mae Sot at 9.2 for ฿700 (cleanliness 9.7).

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget Tak hotels cost?
faq.a: In this guide, prices start around ฿450–780/night. The cheapest are Silayok Grand ฿450, Pingview ฿500, B2 Mae Sot ฿550, RETRO Twin Home ฿576 and Suansin Garden ฿650; around ฿700 you'll find Berich ฿690, Hop Inn ฿700, Moeimanee ฿700, Tak Andaman ฿750 and One Budget ฿780. All are approximate from-rates out of peak season; rates rise and rooms fill fast around festival periods such as the year-end Loi Krathong Sai in Tak town.

faq.q: ❓ On a budget in Tak, where should I stay — Tak town or Mae Sot?
faq.a: It depends on your plans. Riverside Tak town suits town sightseeing, a stopover on a drive north, or sleeping central within a walk of the river and market (Berich, Silayok in town · Tak Andaman, Pingview, Suansin on the edge/riverside, car needed). Mae Sot district suits cross-border errands, the Rim Moei market, or a base before Umphang, with the most — and newest — budget stays in the province (Hop Inn, B2, One Budget in town · Moeimanee, RETRO on the edge).

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a car to do Tak on a budget?
faq.a: Tak has no metro and little public transport. If you stay in central Tak town (Silayok, Berich) or central Mae Sot (Hop Inn, B2, One Budget), you can walk to some food. But the edge-of-town and riverside stays — Tak Andaman, Pingview, Suansin (Tak side) and Moeimanee, RETRO Twin Home (Mae Sot side) — sit outside the shopping areas with few nearby eateries that close early, so a private or rental car is by far the most practical and flexible option, especially if you're continuing to Mae Sot or Umphang.

faq.q: ❓ Are there budget Tak stays with a pool?
faq.a: In this set, the budget 2–3-star stays mostly don't have a pool, as they focus on clean rooms and value. If a pool matters and your budget can stretch a little, Tak has options like White House Hotel (Tak town) and the 4-star Centara Life Mae Sot, priced a notch above this set — see our 12 Popular Tak Hotels guide. As for Tak Andaman, pool info differs by site, so confirm directly with the hotel before booking.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Tak hotels?
faq.a: Prices differ across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com depending on each site's promotions, so open and compare all three before booking — all 10 stays in this guide can be booked and price-compared on all three, and every review page includes the comparison links. It can save tens to hundreds of baht a night, especially around festivals when rooms in Tak town and Mae Sot fill fast.
